selection_reason: No experiments have been run, so the main uncertainty is whether a basic multimodal pipeline is viable and how much signal the standard RNA and image features provide. config_016 tests the simplest full multimodal baseline—PCA RNA, ResNet image, single profile, and concatenation—without confounding advanced encoders, multiprofile aggregation, or weighted fusion. It gives a clear reference point for later one-factor extensions and for comparison with unimodal baselines, making it an efficient first experiment under a limited budget.

The only completed experiment is a multimodal single-profile PCA+ResNet50 model with validation accuracy 0.527 and F1 0.510, which is too sparse to determine whether multimodality is actually helping. Testing config_010, an image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolates the contribution of the image modality while keeping the image encoder and profile setting aligned with config_016. If image-only performs similarly, RNA PCA may be adding little; if it performs much worse, the multimodal result is more promising and justifies further exploration of fusion and RNA encoders. This is a high-information baseline under a limited budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that multimodal PCA+ResNet50 concat substantially outperforms image-only, making this multimodal base promising. The key uncertainty is whether using multiple profiles with simple aggregation can improve on the single-profile result. config_018 keeps the proven RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method while testing multiprofile with avgpool, directly probing an important design choice. This is a good use of the next budget because it exploits the current best direction while clarifying whether profile aggregation is worth pursuing.

The strongest evidence so far is config_018, where multimodal multiprofile with PCA, ResNet, avgpool, and concat reaches 0.619 accuracy and 0.610 F1, clearly above singleprofile multimodal and image-only baselines. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation can improve over avgpool while keeping the other currently best settings fixed. It is the best next step because it directly extends the most promising configuration, isolates the key multiprofile aggregation choice, and will clarify whether a more expressive aggregation method is worth further exploration.

The observed best is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet, avgpool, concat; acc 0.6186, F1 0.6103), with lower performance for singleprofile concat and transformer aggregation, and weak image-only singleprofile. This supports multiprofile avgpool multimodal as a promising direction, but leaves uncertainty about whether weighted fusion can outperform concat in that same setting. config_019 changes only fusion from concat to weighted, directly testing that design choice while retaining the strongest profile/aggregation/encoder evidence. It is a high-value, low-risk exploitation step with high expected accuracy, making it the best use of the next limited-budget experiment.

The strongest evidence is that multimodal multiprofile with PCA, avgpool, and weighted fusion is the best-performing family so far, with config_019 reaching 0.639 validation accuracy and 0.620 F1. The image encoder is an important untested factor in this best family, and the image-only ResNet50 baseline was weak, suggesting that a stronger pretrained image encoder may help the image branch contribute more effectively. config_025 tests exactly this by keeping the proven multiprofile avgpool weighted PCA setup and replacing ResNet50 with imagenet_vit_l. It is the best next experiment because it directly exploits the current strongest direction while clarifying whether image-encoder quality is a key source of remaining performance.

The strongest evidence is multimodal multiprofile with PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion, while transformer+concat is weaker and weighted+avgpool is better than concat+avgpool. config_021 tests the missing transformer+weighted cell, clarifying whether the avgpool advantage over transformer is robust or an interaction with fusion. This is a low-risk, high-information extension of the current best region and avoids overinterpreting the small ResNet vs ViT difference.

The strongest evidence favors multimodal multiprofile with avgpool and weighted fusion: config_019 is best (0.639 acc, 0.620 F1), config_025 is close with a different image encoder, and transformer aggregation is consistently worse. The major untested design choice is the RNA encoder, since all strong results use PCA. config_043 keeps the current best architecture but replaces PCA with scgpt, directly testing whether a pretrained RNA encoder can improve over the PCA baseline. This is the best next experiment because it is a one-variable extension of the most promising region and efficiently reduces uncertainty about an important modality-specific design decision.

The strongest evidence is for multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, especially config_019 (acc 0.639, F1 0.620). ViT is not clearly better than ResNet50, and scGPT performed poorly, but scVI remains untested in the best-supported architecture. This experiment isolates the RNA-encoder choice by keeping the current best multimodal multiprofile ResNet50/avgpool/weighted setting fixed, clarifying whether scVI can improve on PCA or whether PCA should be retained.

The strongest evidence is config_031: multimodal multiprofile with scvi_n200, ResNet50, avgpool, and weighted fusion achieved the best validation accuracy and F1. The main remaining uncertainty in this promising region is whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can further improve performance, since PCA-based ViT was only marginally below PCA-based ResNet under the same aggregation and fusion. config_037 tests this by changing only the image encoder from ResNet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping the best-known RNA encoder, profile setting, aggregation, and fusion fixed. This is the best next use of budget because it exploits the current best direction with a single-factor extension, has high expected performance, and clarifies whether image encoder choice matters for the scvi_n200 multimodal design.
